contradictions.subject: CIAD-2026-0037 entry availability

claim_a.value: not-found body at supplied non-www host

claim_b.value: full advisory at canonical www host

contradictions.resolution: Retain the broken original artifact and use the authoritative www sibling; identifier and servlet path match exactly.

contradictions.subject: ROPC behavior under correctly enforced MFA

claim_a.value: broad wording that ROPC bypasses MFA and Conditional Access

claim_b.value: ROPC cannot perform MFA; users required to perform MFA are blocked

contradictions.resolution: Do not use a universal MFA-bypass claim. Successful access is configuration- and rollout-dependent: noninteractive ROPC cannot satisfy MFA, so correctly applied MFA blocks it; observed compromises had enforcement gaps.

contradictions.subject: Downstream impact after credential compromise

claim_a.value: CERT-In describes campaigns leading to BEC and data exfiltration

claim_b.value: Huntress did not observe post-compromise activity in the LSHIY cohort

contradictions.resolution: The statements are campaign-scoped, not mutually exclusive. Retain the LSHIY non-observation while using CERT-In and Microsoft evidence for credible outcomes in other observed identity-compromise campaigns.

remediation.target: OneDrive for Business, SharePoint Online, and Microsoft Entra ID
remediation.action: Issue an investigation/configuration ticket, not a software patch ticket, unless a separate authoritative source identifies a CVE and fixed build.
prerequisites: confirm SharePoint Online versus SharePoint Server
remediation.restart_or_outage: No restart; control enforcement and containment can interrupt user and automation access.
remediation.rollback: Configuration rollback only after security review.

remediation.action: Inventory device-code use; deploy the Authentication Flows block in report-only mode with audited emergency/dependency exclusions; validate and enable.
remediation.restart_or_outage: No restart; legitimate device-code clients may fail or require fresh tokens.
remediation.rollback: Return the policy to report-only or disabled through approved change control.

remediation.action: Inventory password-grant clients and migrate user automation to interactive modern authentication or workload identities; do not equate this with legacy-client blocking.
remediation.restart_or_outage: ROPC-dependent automation will fail after enforcement.
remediation.rollback: Time-limited owned exception with expiry and compensating controls.

remediation.action: Block legacy authentication for all users and resources using documented client-app conditions after report-only validation.
remediation.restart_or_outage: Legacy clients and dependent automation lose access.
remediation.rollback: Stage by group or temporarily return to report-only while dependencies migrate.

remediation.target: administrators, privileged users, then broader Microsoft 365 users
remediation.action: Register phishing-resistant credentials and stage enforcement of the built-in phishing-resistant MFA strength.
remediation.restart_or_outage: Unregistered or unsupported users/devices will be denied.
remediation.rollback: Remove only the affected cohort under an approved, expiring exception.

remediation.target: suspected compromised identities and rogue devices
remediation.action: Preserve evidence; disable compromised users and suspected devices; revoke sessions; review MFA methods, consents, roles, mail rules, and service activity; restore only after validation.
remediation.restart_or_outage: Immediate user disruption is expected; access-token or application-cookie persistence can outlive session revocation.
remediation.rollback: Re-enable only after identity proofing, credential reset, device validation, and log review.

remediation.target: SharePoint Online and OneDrive for Business
remediation.action: Set organization and site sharing to the least-permissive business-valid level; remove unnecessary anonymous links; review guests, groups, and site admins.
prerequisites: inventory of guests, links, groups, and sensitive sites
remediation.restart_or_outage: No restart; guest and anonymous-link access may be removed after propagation.
remediation.rollback: Restore only specific approved collaboration paths.

remediation.action: Correlate suspicious successful device-code sign-ins, token refreshes, service grants, mailbox access, rules/forwarding changes, outbound-mail cadence, and the immutable Kali365 indicator artifact.
remediation.restart_or_outage: None for read-only hunting; containment requires separate incident authorization.
remediation.rollback: Not applicable for read-only evidence collection.

remediation.title: Investigate Microsoft 365 identity-compromise exposure and harden OneDrive/SharePoint access
remediation.target: OneDrive for Business, SharePoint Online, Microsoft Entra ID, and SharePoint Server deployment-mode clarification
remediation.restart_or_outage: No restart for investigation or SaaS control changes; enforcement and containment can interrupt users, clients, automation and sharing workflows.
remediation.rollback: Use approved configuration rollback, owned expiring exceptions, and validated identity/device restoration only.

verification.acceptance_test: Filter sign-in logs for Authentication Protocol=Device code; during pilot confirm report-only impact, then after enforcement confirm unapproved tests are blocked by the intended policy.
verification.expected_result: No successful unauthorized device-code sign-ins; every permitted use case has an owner and exception.

verification.acceptance_test: Inventory password-grant sign-ins; confirm migrated apps store no user passwords and operate with an approved flow; an MFA-required test user must not obtain a token through ROPC.
verification.expected_result: No production user automation depends on ROPC outside owned expiring exceptions.

verification.acceptance_test: Confirm target users registered a supported method; review report-only results; after enforcement inspect authentication details.
verification.expected_result: In-scope users satisfy phishing-resistant MFA; weaker methods are denied.

verification.acceptance_test: Confirm account disabled, sessions revoked, suspected devices disabled, and application-managed sessions reviewed through at least the normal access-token lifetime.
verification.expected_result: No new tokens, sign-ins, or continuing OneDrive/SharePoint access from the identity or rogue device.

verification.acceptance_test: Correlate device registration/audit events with user, time, device IDs, IP, authentication context, compliance, and management state.
verification.expected_result: Every retained device has an approved owner and enrollment path; unexplained devices are disabled and escalated before deletion.

verification.acceptance_test: Search and export the incident window for file access/download/sync/search, sharing/link, permission, and site-admin changes; wait at least 90 minutes and re-query before treating absence as meaningful.
verification.expected_result: Attributable timeline of content, links, recipients, permissions, IPs, and actors, with telemetry gaps named.

verification.scope: SharePoint admin center and affected sites/OneDrives
verification.acceptance_test: Confirm OneDrive is no more permissive than SharePoint, sensitive sites disallow external sharing, and anonymous links, guests, site admins, and broken inheritance match approved policy.
verification.expected_result: Effective settings and audit events match the approved least-privilege design.

verification.acceptance_test: Confirm deployment mode distinguishes SharePoint Online from SharePoint Server and no source in this graph identifies a CVE or fixed build before issuing a patch ticket.
verification.expected_result: Microsoft 365 identity/configuration investigation ticket; separate server patch work only if independently evidenced.

verification.acceptance_test: Search successful sign-ins for individual CSV IPs and ASN 132203; correlate with device-code protocol, python-requests, token grants, user context, and mailbox behavior. Do not use the disputed aggregate CIDR for automatic blocking.
verification.expected_result: Only behaviorally corroborated matches are escalated; shared-cloud IP matches alone remain leads.

verification.acceptance_test: Review refresh grants without interactive sign-in, service-scoped grants, unusual or Electron agents, file/mailbox access, and linear draft/send/delete cadence.
verification.expected_result: Suspicious sessions are tied to a user, IP, app, resource, and timeline; a common Microsoft client ID alone is not malicious.

verification.acceptance_test: For suspicious accounts, inspect OneDrive/SharePoint token grants, downloads, sharing, and administrative changes during the compromise window.
verification.expected_result: Applicability changes from under_investigation only with tenant and account evidence.

decisions.decision: Treat OneDrive and SharePoint as product-level context only; do not declare environmental applicability without inventory evidence.
decisions.rationale: The input names products but supplies no asset identifiers, deployment modes, versions/builds, or configurations.

decisions.decision: Use the public www.cert-in.org.in sibling as the authoritative entry while preserving the broken supplied URL.
decisions.rationale: The original non-www host returned a not-found body; the www host returned CIAD-2026-0037 with an exact identifier/path match and full advisory content.

decisions.decision: Treat the case as a threat/configuration exposure investigation rather than a CVE patch case unless vendor evidence introduces a patchable flaw.
decisions.rationale: The advisory describes identity attacks and configuration gaps, lists no CVE or affected/fixed build, and recommends tenant controls and hunting.

decisions.decision: Reject a universal 'ROPC bypasses MFA' formulation.
decisions.rationale: Microsoft states MFA-required users are blocked because ROPC cannot perform MFA; successful campaign access occurred where Conditional Access enforcement did not cover the request.

decisions.decision: Keep LSHIY, Kali365, EvilTokens, and Storm-2949 observations source-scoped; do not merge indicators or victim outcomes across campaigns.
decisions.rationale: The sources cover related techniques but distinct observed operations, infrastructure, and impact boundaries.

decisions.decision: Produce an investigation/configuration ticket, not a patch ticket.
decisions.rationale: No CVE, affected version, or fixed build exists in the advisory graph, and environmental applicability cannot be proven from product labels alone.

decisions.decision: Do not silently choose the Kali365 /20 or /18 CIDR and do not use either aggregate for automatic production blocking.
decisions.rationale: The article and its directly linked immutable CSV conflict materially on address-space size; individual indicators require behavioral correlation.

decisions.decision: Record CISA KEV as not applicable, while retaining active exploitation as a campaign-state finding.
decisions.rationale: The advisory graph contains no CVE; KEV is CVE-based and does not express the seriousness of non-CVE identity campaigns.

decisions.decision: Close the public-evidence investigation with an investigation/configuration ticket and named re-check triggers.
decisions.rationale: Required role coverage is sufficient; remaining material questions require private tenant evidence, publisher clarification or unpublished data, and the remaining public frontier has lower expected value.
